html:
SMTO-EXE-0049 — SMTO can't find a USB or external drive to save to

GUID: 6fa68f73-ec89-4887-a537-de655b10d52c
Slug: removable-destination-absent
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to save to a USB or external drive, but it couldn't find one that is plugged in and ready on the computer doing the work. Nothing was written.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Plug the USB or external drive into the computer running the Gateway you picked for this task (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands there). SMTO only looks for drives on that computer, not on the device you are typing on.
  2. On that computer, open the drive in the file browser to confirm it is mounted, and make sure it isn't locked or set to read-only. SMTO skips drives that aren't mounted or can't be written to.
  3. Open the Target menu for this conversation, select Refresh targets, and make sure the computer with the drive is the one chosen. If a different computer is selected, SMTO is looking for the drive in the wrong place.
  4. Ask SMTO to save to the drive again. Nothing was written the first time, so it is safe to try again once the drive is ready.

What success looks like

  • SMTO saves the file to the drive, or asks you which drive to use.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer; the drive may be outside the folders SMTO is allowed to use. Don't pick a different computer or drive just to get past this unless that's where you really want the file.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Removable-destination resolution found no eligible mounted removable destination on the selected Gateway (no writable, mounted, removable or USB device inside the File path policy), so the write was not dispatched.

What this means

  • Removable-destination resolution found no eligible mounted rows from which to choose the required destination. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Removable-destination resolution found no eligible mounted rows from which to choose the required destination.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current removable-device inventory on the selected Gateway, including mount and identity eligibility.

How to fix it

  • On the selected Linux Gateway, confirm the device is mounted read-write, is detected as removable or USB in sysfs, is writable by the Gateway's OS account and lies inside the Gateway's File path policy; then re-request so the guard observes it and binds that exact mount. Do not let the task switch to a different Gateway or drive than the one the user intended.
  • Inspect the intended Gateway and mount the intended removable device through supported host controls. Select its verified identity before requesting a write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended device is mounted and its exact identity is selected before the write is authorized.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
